title: At the Doctor's
subtitle: Describe symptoms clearly
description: Practice the phrases you need to communicate effectively during a medical appointment. Being able to describe how you feel and ask the right questions can make a real difference to your care.
tip: Use the pattern 'I've been + -ing' to describe ongoing symptoms — it sounds more precise and natural than just saying 'I have pain'.
phrases: I've been having a sharp pain in my lower back for the past three days.
The pain gets worse when I sit down for a long time.
I'm allergic to penicillin — is that going to be a problem?
I've been feeling really fatigued and short of breath lately.
Could you explain what this medication is for and how I should take it?
Are there any side effects I should watch out for?
I'd like to schedule a follow-up in about two weeks, if that's possible.
Should I be worried, or is this something that will clear up on its own?
